title: Introduction to Organic Chemistry
content:
# Introduction to Organic Chemistry

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Define organic chemistry and organic compounds
- Explain why carbon forms so many compounds
- Recognise the different types of formulae used in organic chemistry
- Understand homologous series and functional groups

## Introduction

**Organic chemistry** is the study of carbon compounds. Despite being just one element, carbon forms more compounds than all other elements combined. This is because of carbon's unique bonding properties.

## Key Concepts

### Why Carbon is Special

**Carbon's bonding properties:**
- Carbon has 4 electrons in its outer shell
- It can form 4 covalent bonds
- It can bond to other carbon atoms
- It can form chains, rings, and branches

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Valency | 4 (forms 4 bonds) |
| Chain formation | C-C-C-C-C... |
| Branching | Side chains possible |
| Ring formation | Can form cyclic structures |
| Multiple bonds | Can form C=C and C≡C |

### Types of Carbon Compounds

**Hydrocarbons:**
- Contain only hydrogen and carbon
- Examples: methane (CH₄), ethene (C₂H₄)

**Other organic compounds:**
- Contain carbon, hydrogen, and other elements (O, N, S, halogens)
- Examples: ethanol (C₂H₅OH), ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH)

### Types of Formulae

| Type | Example (ethanol) | What it shows |
|------|-------------------|---------------|
| Molecular formula | C₂H₆O | Number of each type of atom |
| Structural formula | CH₃CH₂OH | How atoms are arranged |
| Displayed formula | [Full diagram] | All bonds shown |
| Skeletal formula | [Simplified] | Carbon backbone only |

[DIAGRAM: Displayed formula of ethanol showing all C-H and C-O bonds]

### Homologous Series

**A homologous series is:**
- A family of compounds with the same functional group
- A general formula
- Similar chemical properties
- Gradually changing physical properties

**Key homologous series:**

| Series | General formula | Functional group | Example |
|--------|-----------------|------------------|---------|
| Alkanes | CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ | None (C-C only) | Methane CH₄ |
| Alkenes | CₙH₂ₙ | C=C double bond | Ethene C₂H₄ |
| Alcohols | CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH | -OH (hydroxyl) | Ethanol C₂H₅OH |
| Carboxylic acids | CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH | -COOH (carboxyl) | Ethanoic acid CH₃COOH |

### Functional Groups

**A functional group is:**
- The part of the molecule that determines its chemical properties
- The reactive part of the molecule

| Functional group | Structure | Found in |
|------------------|-----------|----------|
| Hydroxyl | -OH | Alcohols |
| Carboxyl | -COOH | Carboxylic acids |
| Carbon-carbon double bond | C=C | Alkenes |
| Ester link | -COO- | Esters |
| Amine | -NH₂ | Amines |

### Naming Organic Compounds

**Stem indicates chain length:**

| Prefix | Carbon atoms | Example |
|--------|--------------|--------|
| Meth- | 1 | Methane |
| Eth- | 2 | Ethane |
| Prop- | 3 | Propane |
| But- | 4 | Butane |
| Pent- | 5 | Pentane |
| Hex- | 6 | Hexane |

**Suffix indicates homologous series:**

| Suffix | Series | Example |
|--------|--------|---------|
| -ane | Alkanes | Propane |
| -ene | Alkenes | Propene |
| -ol | Alcohols | Propanol |
| -oic acid | Carboxylic acids | Propanoic acid |
| -oate | Esters | Propyl ethanoate |

### Saturated vs Unsaturated

| Type | Bonding | Example |
|------|---------|--------|
| Saturated | Only single C-C bonds | Alkanes |
| Unsaturated | Contains C=C double bonds | Alkenes |

**Saturated compounds:**
- Have maximum hydrogen atoms
- Cannot undergo addition reactions

**Unsaturated compounds:**
- Have fewer hydrogen atoms
- Can undergo addition reactions

## Worked Examples

**Example 1:** How many covalent bonds can one carbon atom form? Explain why.

**Solution:**
- Carbon can form **4 covalent bonds**
- Carbon has 4 electrons in its outer shell
- It needs 4 more electrons to achieve a full outer shell (8 electrons)
- Each covalent bond involves sharing one pair of electrons
- Therefore, carbon forms 4 bonds

---

**Example 2:** Write the molecular formula for a compound with:
- 3 carbon atoms
- Part of the alkane series

**Solution:**
- General formula for alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂
- Where n = 3 (number of carbons)
- Hydrogen atoms = 2(3) + 2 = 8
- Molecular formula: **C₃H₈** (propane)

---

**Example 3:** Identify the homologous series for each compound:
a) C₄H₁₀
b) C₃H₆
c) C₂H₅OH
d) CH₃COOH

**Solution:**
a) C₄H₁₀: Fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ where n=4 → **Alkane** (butane)
b) C₃H₆: Fits CₙH₂ₙ where n=3 → **Alkene** (propene)
c) C₂H₅OH: Contains -OH group → **Alcohol** (ethanol)
d) CH₃COOH: Contains -COOH group → **Carboxylic acid** (ethanoic acid)

---

**Example 4:** Explain the difference between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons.

**Solution:**
**Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes):**
- Contain only single carbon-carbon bonds
- Each carbon is bonded to maximum number of hydrogens
- Cannot undergo addition reactions
- Example: C₂H₆ (ethane)

**Unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes):**
- Contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond (C=C)
- Have fewer hydrogen atoms
- Can undergo addition reactions
- Example: C₂H₄ (ethene)

## Common Mistakes

- **Mistake:** Thinking organic means "natural" or "healthy"
- **Correct:** Organic chemistry means carbon-based chemistry; many organic compounds are synthetic

- **Mistake:** Confusing molecular and structural formulae
- **Correct:** Molecular shows numbers only; structural shows arrangement

- **Mistake:** Forgetting that carbon always makes 4 bonds
- **Correct:** Count bonds in displayed formulae - carbon always has 4

## Practice Questions

1. State two reasons why carbon can form so many compounds. (2 marks)

2. Write the molecular formula for an alkene with 5 carbon atoms. (2 marks)

3. Draw the displayed formula of methane (CH₄). (2 marks)

4. What is a homologous series? Give two features of compounds in a homologous series. (3 marks)

5. Name the functional group in:
   a) Alcohols (1 mark)
   b) Carboxylic acids (1 mark)
   c) Alkenes (1 mark)

6. Explain why ethane (C₂H₆) is described as saturated but ethene (C₂H₄) is unsaturated. (3 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Organic chemistry | The study of carbon compounds |
| Hydrocarbon | A compound containing only carbon and hydrogen |
| Homologous series | A family of compounds with the same functional group and general formula |
| Functional group | The atom or group of atoms that determines chemical properties |
| Saturated | Contains only single carbon-carbon bonds |
| Unsaturated | Contains at least one carbon-carbon double bond |
| Molecular formula | Shows the number of each type of atom in a molecule |

## Summary

- **Organic chemistry** is the study of carbon compounds
- **Carbon forms 4 bonds** - can make chains, branches, and rings
- **Homologous series** - families with same functional group (alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids)
- **General formulae:** Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, Alkenes CₙH₂ₙ
- **Naming:** Prefix (chain length) + suffix (series)
- **Saturated** = single bonds only; **Unsaturated** = contains C=C
